trades.model_hook: assumptions_for_bus_voltage at 540, 756, 800, 1,000 V, with and without DC-DC
trades.note: Voltage and cell series count are one decision; the engine-out battery voltage limit binds
trades.precedent: X-57 hit interference between its inverters and onboard systems and redesigned its battery for overheating; integration problems and component shortages ended the programme before first flight.
sources: NASA: X-57 project creates paths toward electric aviation
trades.block0_choice: The bus voltage native to the selected machines and inverters, fixed by month 2

trades.label: Tilt mechanism: spindle station, bearings and fitting concept
trades.note: Sets whirl flutter, jump take-off root strain and nacelle CG against the elastic axis
trades.precedent: V-22 tilts the whole nacelle: engine, gearbox and rotor. V-280 keeps the engines fixed and tilts only the proprotor gearbox; Bell cites maintenance (engine, shaft and gearbox removable independently) and says the V-280 weighs less than a V-22. Halo already keeps the turbines in the fuselage and tilts only motors, gearbox and rotor, the V-280 logic carried further.
sources: The War Zone: V-280 against V-22, with Bell's head of tiltrotor systems
trades.block0_choice: Conservative machined spindle and fittings with generous margin; nacelles locked at 90 deg for first flight

trades.label: Failure architecture: interconnect shaft or electrical cross-strapping
trades.note: Needs asymmetric failure cases with roll trim
trades.precedent: XV-15 and V-22 both carry a cross-shaft so one engine drives both rotors; V-280 kept it. No tiltrotor that has flown has replaced the shaft with electrical cross-strapping, so Halo's choice carries certification risk as well as mass.
sources: The War Zone: V-280 against V-22, with Bell's head of tiltrotor systems
trades.block0_choice: Electrical cross-strapping as designed; the uncrewed test article carries the risk with flight termination. Shaft question goes to the certification authority for Block 1

trades.note: The actuator is the pylon pitch spring for whirl flutter; a jam is a critical failure
trades.precedent: V-22: a three-bar linkage with a linear actuator, two hydraulic motors and an electric third for triple redundancy; the nacelle is locked horizontal to unload the actuator. Joby JAS4-2: the NTSB named the tilt actuator linkage at one station, which let blades run steeper than commanded, as a contributing factor in a cascading prototype loss.

trades.label: Whirl-flutter margin: frequency placement or flutter-speed margin
trades.note: Frequency placement is a proxy the reference meets while fluttering at 262 kt against 302 kt (plan 040). Plan 055 sizes against the calibrated flutter speed directly: +393 lb on stiffness alone (gap.whirl_flutter); recommended margin policy: 1.15 V_D on the calibrated flutter speed
trades.precedent: XV-15 and V-22 use 23 % thick wings to keep whirl flutter beyond dive speed, at a drag and speed cost; a 15 % NASA design lost stiffness, and tailoring recovered stability at about 18 %. Halo's NACA 2423 follows the same precedent.
sources: Acree, Peyran and Johnson, NASA/TP-2004-212262 (thin-wing whirl flutter), as reported
trades.block0_choice: Frequency placement with wide margin; airplane-mode speed limited until flutter is cleared
